column1: # EXECUTED-SURFACE MANIFEST — every flag corral exposes, and whether anything
# WHY IT EXISTS. `--jail container` was advertised in the README as the
# macOS/Windows path and had never been executed once. It was broken in the
# most basic way available: docker mounts --tmpfs noexec, Go compiles its test
# binary into /tmp and execs it, so every run died as COULD-NOT-GRADE. A claim
# written from intent rather than from a run is indistinguishable, on the page,
# from one that was earned. This file is the difference.
# An exposed flag is a promise whether or not anyone documented it, so the
# enumeration is every flag in docs/cli/*.md — which scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh
# --check guarantees is what the binaries really print.
#   executed    something ran it. The receipt names WHAT: `test:<file>` or
#   attested    executed, but not reproducible in CI, and the reason is not
#               "nobody got round to it": it costs money per run (paid model
#               seats) or it has an irreversible public side effect
#               A missing macOS or Windows runner is NOT this — GitHub offers
#               both free to public repos, so those are unexecuted with a task
#   unexecuted  no test passes it and no recorded run used it. LEGAL, and the
#               point: the manifest does not demand everything be proven, it
#               demands you know. The companion rule is that nothing marked
#               unexecuted may appear in a user-facing claim.
# WHAT A `test:` RECEIPT DOES NOT PROVE. It names a test in the owning binary's
# package that passes this flag literal. That is a pointer to read, not proof
# the flag's BEHAVIOUR is asserted — a test may pass a flag and never check
# what it did. Treat it as "someone has been here", and upgrade it to a `run:`
# receipt or a named behavioural test when the surface matters.
# AND IT MISSES THE OPPOSITE CASE, which the first triage pass found the hard
# way. --max-proven-missed was seeded `unexecuted` because no test passes that
# been calling repoScanExitCode with its value directly all along. The flag's
# LOGIC was tested; its parsing was not. So a seeded `unexecuted` means "no
# test passes the literal and no recorded run used it", which is narrower than
# "nothing has ever exercised this". Read a row as a question that has been
# ASKED, not as a measurement — and when you triage one, look for a
# behavioural test before assuming the surface is untouched.
# Regenerate the enumeration, never this file's judgements, with
# TestDocsEverySurfaceIsClassified, which fails on a surface with no row and on a
# row for a surface that no longer exists.
